urgent.ex: She sent an urgent message to her boss.

usually.ex: I usually wake up at six.
usually.mn: usual – jo aam 'use' me aata hai, roz waise hi

utterly.mn: utter-ly – 'utter' matlab poora bol dena, bilkul completely

uncomfortable.mean: causing or feeling unease or discomfort
uncomfortable.ex: The tight shoes were very uncomfortable.
uncomfortable.mn: uncomfortable – comfort na mile to unease

unemployed.ex: He stayed unemployed for six months.
unemployed.mn: unemployed – no employ, ghar par bekaar

uninterruptedly.ex: The machine ran uninterruptedly all night.
uninterruptedly.mn: uninterruptedly – no rupture, lagataar chalta raha

unwearied.ex: Her unwearied efforts finished the project.
unwearied.mn: unwearied – weary nahi, bina thake kaam

unable to function as before.mean: not able to work like before
unable to function as before.bn: আগের মতো কাজ করতে না পারা
unable to function as before.ex: After the fever, Grandpa was unable to function as before.

unable to sleep well.mean: not able to sleep properly at night
unable to sleep well.ex: Priya was unable to sleep well before the maths exam.

undecided on a topic.mean: not sure what to think or choose
undecided on a topic.ex: Sita is undecided on which dress to buy.

under all circumstances.mean: no matter what happens, in every situation
under all circumstances.ex: Rahul will help his friend under all circumstances.

under all conditions.mean: in every kind of situation, good or bad
under all conditions.ex: The bus runs under all conditions, even in heavy rain.

under extreme pressure.ex: Students are under extreme pressure before the board exam.

under her belt.ex: Sita has three medals under her belt.

under suspicion.mean: people think you did something wrong
under suspicion.ex: The boy is under suspicion for breaking the window.

under the weather.mean: feeling a little sick or not well
under the weather.ex: Rahul is under the weather, so he stayed home.

uneducated person.mean: a person who has not gone to school
uneducated person.ex: That uneducated person cannot read the signboard.

unknown paths.mean: roads or ways no one has walked before
unknown paths.ex: The hero walks on unknown paths to find treasure.

unnecessary tension.ex: Rahul created unnecessary tension before the exam.

up a creek without a paddle.mean: in trouble with no help available
up a creek without a paddle.bn: বিপদে পড়া, কোনো সাহায্য না পাওয়া
up a creek without a paddle.ex: Without his notes, Rahul was up a creek without a paddle in the test.

up in a creek without a paddle.ex: When the auto broke down, the family was up in a creek without a paddle.

up in arms.mean: very angry and ready to fight
up in arms.ex: Rahul was up in arms when his cycle was stolen.

up in the air.ex: The cricket match is up in the air because of rain.

up the ante.mean: to increase the challenge or risk
up the ante.ex: Sita upped the ante by studying two extra hours daily.

upset someone's plans.mean: to spoil what someone wanted to do
upset someone's plans.ex: The heavy rain upset our picnic plans for Sunday.

useful for one's purpose.mean: helps you reach your own goal
useful for one's purpose.ex: The old bicycle was useful for Sita's purpose of going to school.

using a gun for sports.mean: shooting practice for fun or competition
using a gun for sports.bn: খেলার জন্য বন্দুক দিয়ে গুলি চালানো
using a gun for sports.ex: Shooting competitions in India use guns for sports.

using a well-known path.ex: We used the well-known path through the market to school.

using wrongful means.mean: doing things in a bad or cheating way
using wrongful means.bn: ভুল বা অন্যায় উপায়ে কাজ করা
using wrongful means.ex: Copying in exams is using wrongful means to get marks.
